purpose: Service review for WUP2025 rank 688 Evaton (city code 3714); source registry evidence and safe anonymous full-polygon access status.
primaryPublisher: Chief Surveyor-General describes its spatial component as a computerized map of South African land parcels and administrative boundaries.
registryBasis: The Chief Surveyor-General’s public cadastral spatial dataset describes a national polygon layer of surveyed parcels and exposes native PRCL_KEY. Official Emfuleni planning material identifies Evaton within Emfuleni Local Municipality. A point-intersects query at the exact WUP locator returned one CSG “Erven” polygon; only PRCL_KEY and geometry were requested.

officialSources.observation: Chief Surveyor-General describes its spatial component as a computerized map of South African land parcels and administrative boundaries.
Chief Surveyor-General lists parcel types including erven and offers a view-spatial-data route.
CSG warns the web cadastral data is beta/not current and that coordinates are not legal values; sample is retained for research only and runtime is not enabled.
Government-hosted CSG “Erven” feature layer metadata declares polygon geometry, EPSG:4148 source extent, public JSON/GeoJSON query support, and string field PRCL_KEY.
Official Emfuleni municipality spatial-development framework names Evaton among its settlements/nodes.

A public Emfuleni-named ArcGIS layer was inspected as a secondary cross-check only; its ArcGIS item owner metadata did not identify a government publisher. A geometry-only point query returned a two-feature boundary intersection, one carrying the same PRCL_KEY; it was not retained as the primary sample.

accessReview.reason: A full polygon sample is available, but the CSG itself states its web spatial dataset is beta and not current; no citywide coverage or source freshness was tested. Runtime remains disabled pending source-quality review.

requestEvidence.observation: The public layer metadata and source-native identifier were inspected before any geometry query.
Public layer metadata declares geometryType esriGeometryPolygon; the Erven layer exposes native field PRCL_KEY (string). No feature rows were requested during schema inspection.

Exact WUP point, EPSG:4326, spatialRel=esriSpatialRelIntersects, outFields=PRCL_KEY, returnGeometry=true, max 3 features. Response contained one Polygon, one closed 8-coordinate ring, point covered, output attributes exactly [PRCL_KEY]. Native key retained in sample.
The Chief Surveyor-General disclaimer calls its web spatial dataset beta/not current and says coordinates are not legal values. Sample is a candidate only; runtime is not enabled.

requestEvidence.method: GET geometry-only point query with f=geojson
requestEvidence.observation: ArcGIS returned a JSON error object (code 400, failed to execute query) and no features. The identical point and field allowlist were retried with f=json, which returned one polygon.

technicalBlocker: One exact-point full polygon sample is verified. The candidate is pending root contract, stable-key identity, bounded-paging and geometry-quality checks. The CSG currentness caveat is recorded for review but does not by itself block qualification.
sampleDisposition: One full geometry-only CSG polygon retained with native PRCL_KEY; pending root contract and quality checks. CSG beta/not-current disclaimer retained as source context.
remainingUncertainty: Root review must confirm provider contract, stable identity behavior, bounded paging and geometry quality; source currentness and citywide coverage remain unverified.

rootRuntimeAssessment.scope: 46 valid distinct Chief Surveyor-General Erven references verified in thirteen bounded 0.001-degree cells around the unchanged Evaton WUP settlement locator. Complete object-ID manifests, forced three-row geometry pages, all 46 fresh native PRCL_KEY reads, explicit absence, footprint and binding passed in 59 requests through the existing strict Esri JSON reader. Independent EPSG:32735 GEOS found no invalid geometries, exact duplicates or operation errors, and one 0.0130704 m² boundary overlap. A fresh original native EPSG:4148 response reproduces that overlap as a strip under one millimetre wide over about 54 metres; both full polygons retain it without repair or exclusion and are accepted for bounded reference use. The publisher states its web dataset is beta/not current and coordinates are not legal values; currentness, legal title, survey accuracy and wider citywide completeness remain unverified.
